summary: Tunisia combines restoration, conservation and agricultural resilience. Integrated programmes aim to restore degraded agricultural, forest and pastoral landscapes across 487,000 hectares by 2030 and 855,000 by 2035, while 1.2 million hectares are to receive conservation, restoration and soil protection. Dune stabilization reaches 100,000 hectares annually, alongside a cumulative 20,000 hectares of semi-forest plantings over 2026–2035. Conservation targets include 480,000 hectares of forest managed with climate risks—about 122% of Tunisia’s 2022 mapped forest area—fire damage limited to 3,000 hectares annually from 2030 and 1,000 thereafter, protection of 315 km of coast, and ecological water for 10 of 42 wetlands. Agriculture targets include 500,000 hectares under organic farming (≈10.5% of agricultural land), 450,000 hectares irrigated at 90% intensification, 725,000 hectares of collective and public grazing land improved, and 510,000 hectares/year of private grazing land. These actions could deliver 22 million tCO2 in reductions and sequestration over 2026–2035.
